correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated all 3^8=6561 complement-compatible edge support choices of the order-three binary de Bruijn graph using two-way reachable vertex tests, found exactly 20 nonempty strongly connected supports with six maximal support sets identical to the listed hexadecimal templates. Every nonconstant support belonged to exactly one maximal set, while 0000 and 1111 singleton loops each lay in three; the correction -4 is necessary. Their determinant polynomials are 1-z-z^7 (four) and 1-z-z^3 (two). A closed walk yields an n-periodic word even for n<4; trace/determinant gives all n; labelled cyclic gaps give p_m(n). Independently enumerated every binary n-word for n<=15 and checked exact c_n; this does not substitute for exhaustive finite SUPPORT classification and transfer algebra supporting infinite n.

value.rationale: The six maximal strongly connected factor-support templates give a complete, unexpectedly small symbolic-dynamical decomposition of a naturally defined forbidden-pair subshift. The resulting exact circular counts, necklaces, primitive periods and zeta are useful intrinsic invariants, not arbitrary finite recomputations.

final_claim: For all n>=1 circular labelled binary words with no complementary pair of cyclic length-four factors, c_n=2p_3(n)+4p_7(n)-4 where p_m(n) counts cyclic words with at least m-1 zeros between ones; the exact dynamical zeta is (1-z)^4/((1-z-z^3)^2(1-z-z^7)^4), with Burnside necklace and Möbius primitive-period formulas and growth c_n~2lambda^n.
limitations: Binary bitwise complement, cyclic length-four factors only, labelled positive n including wraparound n<4; not reverse complement or higher alphabets.
